value.title: Active project identity is stable during database background work
value.statement: Manual and per-account scheduled sync share a serial project queue; sync_all_projects defaults to true and false limits new full runs to the open map. A layer-specific run stays in the open map. The queue holds one DATA_SYNC lease throughout every project, account and async child without changing active preferences, MapBase active identity or drafts. Background maps use scoped lookup, opaque provider/service tokens and tracked callbacks; expired tokens cannot fall back to the UI database. Untagged provider URI remains bound to the active UI map even inside a background scope; map-path-tagged broadcasts have a separate receiving-owner gate. Lease workspaceKey read from active preferences is not the background database binding. Only unclaimed service deliveries have a 60s expiry; claimed work retains ownership until it actually finishes and has no such timeout promise. Only session-owned fill/rebuild stages may join a scoped queue and touch SQLite in its dependent phase. Switch/create/rename/delete and unrelated imports wait for all owners, and duplicate full sync is refused. Cancellation stops reads and rolls back interrupted apply while awaiting unresolved outbound writes and children before releasing their database. The complete durable pair plan survives process death and each successful pair is acknowledged separately. Collector journals are path-partitioned; legacy migration, runtime state, schema guards and draft reservations validate the owning project. An unchanged schema mismatch is circuit-broken after two attempts in 24 hours, with at least ten minutes between attempts, and LayerFillService timeout must preserve the durable import journal. Settings storage move and Reset Settings acquire the existing exclusive PROJECT_SWITCH lease before default-destination resolution or any prefs/render/map/result effect. Busy refusal preserves the held owner and all settings; chooser admission never persists a proposed path. Exact-map retirement precedes physical move but does not prove active renderer read drain. The lease survives worker completion through guarded actual-path map refresh, Reset callbacks and UI cleanup. RESULT_OK requests Activity rebind, not successful storage ACK. Failed target/commit or cancellation after retirement may refresh only the exact owner whose raw cached path equals actual map path; they do not execute Reset defaults or layer deletion. Atomic owner predicate/rebind never resolves a missing map through getMap. Unexpected before-cache failures, partial rollback, restart and workspace-key migration remain separate unaccepted recovery boundaries.
